triples.rationale: Micah describes wrongdoers planning evil on their beds before carrying it out. The psalm likewise depicts the lawless person devising lawlessness upon his bed and refusing the good way.
triples.source_text: They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.

target_units.text: The lawless person speaks within himself of sinning; there is no fear of God before his eyes.
For he acted deceitfully in his sight, as to finding his lawlessness and hating it.
The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit; he was unwilling to understand so as to do good.
He devised lawlessness upon his bed; he stood by every way that was not good, and he was not offended by wickedness.

triples.rationale: Micah condemns coveting fields and plundering a person, house and inheritance. Isaiah likewise condemns joining house to house and field to field in order to take from a neighbor.
triples.source_text: They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

target_units.text: Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field beside field, so that they may take something from their neighbor! Surely you will not dwell alone upon the earth?

triples.rationale: Micah condemns taking a person's field and inheritance. Kings records Ahab going to possess Naboth's vineyard after Naboth's death, following the refusal to surrender his ancestral inheritance in the surrounding account.
triples.source_text: They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

target_units.text: When Jezebel heard, she said to Ahab, “Rise, take possession of Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard, which he did not give you for silver. Naboth is no longer alive; he is dead.”
When Ahab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. After this, Ahab rose and went down to Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard to take possession of it.

triples.rationale: The Lord declares that He is planning calamities against the offending tribe. Jeremiah similarly announces the Lord's shaping evils and devising a design against Judah and Jerusalem, alongside a call to turn from evil practices.
triples.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: “Look, I am planning calamities against this tribe, from which you will certainly not lift your necks, and you will certainly not suddenly walk upright, for it is an evil time.

target_units.text: And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.

triples.relationship: shared loss through division of the people's land
triples.rationale: Micah's lament says the people's portion was measured and their fields divided. Joel condemns nations for scattering Israel and dividing the Lord's land; both describe dispossession through division of the land.
triples.source_text: On that day a parable will be taken up against you, and a lament will be sung in melody, saying: ‘We have suffered grievous misery! The portion of My people was measured with a cord, and there was no one to prevent him from turning away; our fields were divided.’

target_units.text: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land

triples.relationship: loss contrasted with inheritance allotted by lot
triples.rationale: Micah threatens the loss of anyone casting a measuring cord by lot in the Lord's assembly. Joshua's account surveys the land into portions and casts a lot before the Lord, providing the positive allotment practice with which Micah's exclusion contrasts.
triples.source_text: Therefore you will have no one casting a measuring cord by lot in the assembly of the Lord.

target_units.text: The men rose and went. Joshua commanded the men going to survey the land, saying, “Go and survey the land and return to me. Here at Shiloh I will bring out a lot for you before the Lord.”
They went, surveyed the land, saw it, and wrote it by its cities in seven portions in a scroll, which they brought to Joshua.
Joshua cast a lot for them at Shiloh before the Lord.

triples.rationale: Micah cites the claim that Jacob's house provoked the Lord's Spirit. Isaiah describes the people disobeying and provoking His holy spirit, followed by the Lord turning against them. The connection concerns the stated provocation, not an imported claim that God's patience is short.
triples.source_text: The one who says, ‘Jacob’s house has provoked the Lord’s Spirit’: Are these his practices? Are not his words good with him, and have they walked uprightly?

target_units.text: But they disobeyed and provoked His holy spirit. He turned toward hostility against them and Himself fought them.

triples.relationship: same-book imagery of flaying the people
triples.rationale: Micah 2 describes hostility through the image of flaying skin. Chapter 3 develops the charge against leaders with skins stripped from the people and their flesh treated as meat, repeating the book's bodily imagery of abuse.
triples.source_text: And formerly My people stood opposed in enmity; facing his peace, they flayed his skin to take away hope—a shattering of war.

triples.rationale: Micah says the people's leaders will be expelled from luxurious houses because of their practices. Amos likewise describes powerful people reclining on ivory beds and enjoying costly food and perfume, then announces captivity.
triples.source_text: Therefore the leaders of My people will be cast out of their luxurious houses; because of their evil practices they were expelled. Draw near to everlasting mountains!

target_units.text: sleeping upon ivory beds and indulging upon your couches, eating young goats from the flocks and milk-fed calves from the herds,
clapping to the sound of instruments; they reckoned them as lasting, not passing away,
drinking strained wine and anointing yourselves with the finest perfumes, yet suffering nothing over Joseph’s shattering.
Therefore now they will be captives from the foremost of the powerful, and horses’ neighing will be removed from Ephraim.

triples.relationship: uncleanness and loss of a place to remain
triples.rationale: Micah commands departure because uncleanness has made the place no resting place. Leviticus connects defilement of the land with the Lord driving out its inhabitants and warns Israel against the same defilement.
triples.source_text: Rise and go, for this is no resting place for you because of uncleanness. You were corrupted with corruption,

target_units.text: Do not defile yourselves in any of these things; for in all these things the nations whom I drive out before your face were defiled,
and the land became defiled, and I repaid them for wrongdoing because of it, and the land became indignant with those settled upon it.
And you shall keep all My statutes and all My commands, and do none of these abominations, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who has joined himself among you—
for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became defiled—
so that the land is not indignant with you when you defile it, as it was indignant with the nations before you.

triples.rationale: Micah describes being pursued with no one pursuing. Leviticus' covenant sanctions include fleeing when no one pursues, alongside defeat before enemies. The paradoxical pursuit language is the specific connection.

target_units.text: And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.

triples.relationship: Israel gathered and rested as a flock
triples.rationale: Micah promises to gather Jacob and Israel's remaining ones and place them together as sheep in a resting place. Ezekiel likewise promises to gather the sheep from countries, bring them to their land and give them good pasture and rest.
triples.source_text: Jacob will surely be gathered with everyone. I will surely receive Israel’s remaining ones; I will put their turning back together. Like sheep in affliction, like a flock within their resting place, they will leap out from among people.

target_units.text: I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land. I will feed them upon Israel’s mountains, in the ravines and in every dwelling place of the land.
I will feed them in good pasture, and their folds will be upon Israel’s high mountain. There they will lie down, there rest in good delight, and graze in rich pasture upon Israel’s mountains.
I Myself will feed My sheep and give them rest, and they will know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:

triples.relationship: shared flock leadership through an opening
triples.rationale: Micah's gathered flock passes through a gate with its king before it and the Lord leading. John describes the opened sheepfold, the shepherd leading his sheep out and going before them. The connection is the shared leadership image, not a claim that the passages narrate the same event.
triples.source_text: Through the breach before them they broke through, passed a gate and went out through it. Their king went out before them, and the Lord will lead them.”

target_units.text: To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought all his own out, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.

triples.rationale: Micah asks Israel's authorities whether they ought to know justice. Deuteronomy directs appointed judges and officers to judge the people with righteous judgment, supplying the explicit responsibility challenged by the question.
triples.source_text: He will say: “Hear these things now, authorities of Jacob’s house and remaining ones of Israel’s house! Is it not for you to know justice,

target_units.text: You shall appoint judges and recording officers for yourself in all your cities which the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
